_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 12: Record-keeping
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. A harmonised standard on record keeping through logging capabilities by AI systems is being developed by CEN and CENELEC under Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, point 3. No official date for publication of its reference in the Official Journal of the European Union has been announced.
basis: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, controls 8.15 (Logging) and 8.16 (Monitoring activities)
_metadata.awaiting_standard: A harmonised standard on record keeping through logging capabilities by AI systems is being developed by CEN and CENELEC under Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 3871, Annex I, point 3. No official date for publication of its reference in the Official Journal of the European Union has been announced.

requirements.title: Logging Framework Required
requirements.requirement: The high-risk AI system MUST technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system (Article 12(1)). A structured logging framework capable of automatic event recording SHOULD be used; the Regulation does not prescribe a framework.
requirements.rationale: Art. 12(1): 'High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.' Manual logging is not automatic recording; unstructured print statements make the traceability required by Art. 12(2) hard to achieve.
acceptable_implementations: Python: structlog, loguru, stdlib logging with JSON formatter
not_acceptable: Manual log file writing without framework

requirements.title: Logging Coverage
requirements.requirement: At least 90% of API endpoints / entry points SHOULD have structured logging.
requirements.rationale: Art. 12(1) requires the automatic recording of events 'over the lifetime of the system', and Art. 12(2) requires logging capabilities that enable the recording of events relevant for the purposes in points (a) to (c). Entry points without logging may leave such events unrecorded.
requirements.note: The 90% threshold is a ComplianceLint heuristic. The Regulation sets no coverage threshold, and it is not known whether the harmonised standard on logging will set one.

requirements.title: Structured Log Fields
requirements.requirement: Each log entry SHOULD include at minimum: timestamp, event_type, and a correlation identifier (session_id, trace_id, or request_id); the Regulation does not prescribe log fields for high-risk AI systems in general. For high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III, point 1(a), the logging capabilities MUST provide, at a minimum: recording of the period of each use of the system (start date and time and end date and time of each use), the reference database against which input data has been checked by the system, the input data for which the search has led to a match, and the identification of the natural persons involved in the verification of the results, as referred to in Article 14(5) (Article 12(3)).
recommended_fields: input_hash (hash of input data, not raw data)
requirements.rationale: Art. 12(2)(a) requires logging capabilities that enable the recording of events relevant for 'identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) or in a substantial modification'. Structured fields make such events queryable; free-text messages do not. Art. 12(3) sets the minimum log content only for remote biometric identification systems (Annex III, point 1(a)).

requirements.title: Log Retention
requirements.requirement: The provider MUST keep the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, to the extent such logs are under its control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law, in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data (Article 19(1)). Providers that are financial institutions subject to requirements regarding their internal governance, arrangements or processes under Union financial services law MUST maintain the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems as part of the documentation kept under the relevant financial services law (Article 19(2)). Systems in healthcare, law enforcement, or critical infrastructure SHOULD retain logs for 12 months or more, within the limits of applicable data protection law.
requirements.rationale: Art. 19(1) explicitly states 'at least six months.' The Regulation sets no longer period for particular domains; the 12-month period is a ComplianceLint recommendation, not a requirement.
implementation_guidance: Configure log rotation that keeps logs for 184 days (at least six months)
Use append-only log storage (S3 with object lock, WORM storage)
Ensure retention policy is documented and auditable
Consider GDPR data minimization: anonymize personal data in logs after active use period

requirements.title: Log Integrity / Tamper Protection
requirements.requirement: Logs SHOULD be protected against tampering. The Regulation does not expressly require tamper protection for any high-risk AI system, including those referred to in Annex III, point 1(a).
requirements.rationale: The Regulation does not expressly require tamper protection. Art. 12(2) requires logging that ensures 'a level of traceability of the functioning of a high-risk AI system that is appropriate to the intended purpose of the system', and Recital 71 links logs to traceability; logs that can be altered after the fact support traceability less well.
acceptable_implementations: Hash chain (each log entry includes hash of previous entry)
Append-only storage (S3 Object Lock, Azure Immutable Blob)
requirements.note: Art. 12(3) sets the minimum content of the logs of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III, point 1(a) (see IS-ART12-R03); it does not require tamper protection. Tamper protection is a ComplianceLint recommendation for all high-risk AI systems.

requirements.title: Log Accessibility for Deployers
requirements.requirement: The logging capabilities MUST enable the recording of events relevant for monitoring the operation of the high-risk AI system referred to in Article 26(5) (Article 12(2)(c)). The provider SHOULD offer deployers a mechanism to access the logs or log summaries relevant to that monitoring. Where relevant, the instructions for use MUST describe the mechanisms included within the system that allow deployers to properly collect, store and interpret the logs (Article 13(3)(f)).
requirements.rationale: Art. 12(2)(c) requires logging capabilities that enable the recording of events relevant for 'monitoring the operation of high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 26(5)', and Art. 13(3)(f) requires, where relevant, 'a description of the mechanisms included within the high-risk AI system that allows deployers to properly collect, store and interpret the logs in accordance with Article 12'. The Regulation does not prescribe a specific access mechanism.
acceptable_implementations: Log forwarding to deployer's SIEM/logging system

scoring.compliant: The MUST parts of R01, R04 and R06 met, and, for high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III, point 1(a), the MUST part of R03 met (R02, R05 and the SHOULD parts of R01, R03, R04 and R06 are recommended, not required)
scoring.partial: The MUST part of R01 met, but the MUST part of R04 or R06, or, where it applies, of R03 not met
scoring.non_compliant: The MUST part of R01 not met
